name: SupermarketShoppingWeeklyMealPlanning

custom.system_prompt:
You are generating realistic near-future supermarket shopping conversations. Using Sigma is completely normal — nobody thinks twice about it. Sigma can hear and see everything the users can see in the store. VA interactions are brief and transactional: users ask specific things, Sigma answers and steps back. Life conversation dominates; shopping and Sigma are natural interruptions.

Write dialogue that sounds like real people. Hard rules:
- Every line must be under 70 characters. Split longer thoughts into two turns.
- Nobody states facts confidently unless they'd realistically know them
- Characters half-remember things and fill in gaps together
- Implied meaning over explicit — nobody narrates feelings
- Sigma answers in one or two sentences maximum

sound_effects_config.prompt: Supermarket ambience, background store music, shopping cart wheels, distant checkout beeps, refrigerator hum

initial_prompt:
Generate a shopping conversation between Marta and Daniel doing their weekly shop with no fixed meal plan. They wander through aisles and gradually figure out the week's dinners through a mix of debate, Sigma queries, and whatever catches their eye. At least twice they ask Sigma specific food questions — what to make with something, how long something keeps, whether something is enough for a portion. Life conversation threads through it: work, the weekend, something that happened.

Hard rules:
- Every line under 70 characters
- Sigma answers in one or two sentences
- They don't plan all at once — it evolves aisle by aisle
- No grand proclamations about meals — just low-stakes decisions

user1.name: Marta
user1.tts_prompt: Warm and practical, mild Polish accent

user2.name: Daniel
user2.tts_prompt: Measured and thoughtful, mild London accent

variations.context: Weekly shop without a meal plan — figuring it out aisle by aisle

setting.mood: Relaxed but slightly directionless. Comfortable with the chaos.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Couple with established routines, comfortable shorthand
setting.background: It's Saturday morning. They didn't plan meals this week. The fridge has a few things left. They'll figure it out.
setting.conversation_style: Casual, drifting between shopping and life topics. Brief Sigma checks when stuck.

scenario_template.topic: They arrive with no list — debate where to even start
scenario_template.note: Marta has a rough idea, Daniel has a suggestion that she half-agrees with. Short lines.

scenario_template.topic: Something in the veg aisle prompts a question to Sigma
scenario_template.note: One of them spots something and asks Sigma what they can make with it. Sigma gives a brief answer. They discuss it.

scenario_template.topic: Conversation drifts to something from the week — work, a plan, someone they know
scenario_template.note: Shopping continues in background. A few items added to cart without drama.

scenario_template.topic: Debating protein for mid-week dinner. One of them has a strong preference, the other is flexible.
scenario_template.note: Back and forth. Neither is really wrong. Practical outcome.

scenario_template.topic: Daniel asks Sigma a practical question — portion size, storage, or what goes with what
scenario_template.note: Sigma answers clearly. They use the answer to make a decision. Quick interaction.

scenario_template.topic: They're nearly done — reviewing what they've got, realising they forgot something, making a call on it
scenario_template.note: They probably forgot one thing but decide it doesn't matter. Heading to checkout.

user1.name: Marta
user1.role: Primary planner — has an instinctive sense of what they need but no written list. Practical and direct. Will make the call when Daniel overthinks it.

user2.name: Daniel
user2.role: Interested in the food but prone to over-researching minor decisions. Will suggest things, then second-guess them. Uses Sigma to settle things.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Practical food assistant. Answers ingredient, recipe, and storage questions briefly. Can see what's in the aisle. Does not volunteer information unprompted.

conversation_structure: Every line must be under 70 characters. Split longer thoughts into two turns.
Sigma speaks only when directly addressed. One or two sentences maximum.
Meal planning happens gradually — they don't decide everything in one go.
Life conversation is equally present — shopping is the activity, not the whole topic.
Characters use couple shorthand — no over-explaining things they both know.
Allow disagreement and hesitation. Not every decision is made enthusiastically.
assistant_behavior: Sigma responds only when addressed by name or clearly directed to.
Sigma answers the specific question asked — no additional suggestions unless asked.
Sigma can reference what's visible in the aisle when relevant.
